title: 공부가 필요할 것 같아서요  (I Thought I Would Need to Study)

segments.t: In his family's study room, rookie producer Baek Seung-chan earnestly explains his homework to the documentary cameraman before receiving his show assignment. Listen for "gongbu", meaning 'study', and "komidi", meaning 'comedy'.
일단 바보 캐릭터를 비교 분석 중인데요.
입을 작게 열고 혀 짧은 소리로 발성을,
Let's unpack those twelve lines one turn at a time.
'I thought I would need to study.' Seung-chan explains his effort using "gongbu", 'study', and "pilyohal geot gataseoyo", 'because it seems it will be needed'.

'I am tracing the history of our country's comedy, you could say.' Seung-chan sets the grand scope with "urinara", 'our country', and "yeoksa", 'history'. He uses "deodeumneun", 'tracing', and softens his nerdy answer with "-iralkka", 'you could say'.

'Please introduce a little bit of what you learned.' The cameraman asks to hear more using "baeun geo", 'what you learned', and "jogeumman", 'just a little'. He formally requests this with "sogaehae juseyo", 'please introduce'.
일단 바보 캐릭터를 비교 분석 중인데요.

'First, I am comparing and analyzing fool characters.' Seung-chan outlines his method with "ildan", 'first', focusing on "babo", 'fool', and "kaerikteo", 'characters'. He is deeply engaged in "bigyo", 'comparison', and "bunseok", 'analysis'.
'There are many differences.' Seung-chan states his finding simply using "chai", 'difference', and "manayo", 'are many'.

'Hello there, while one throws a greeting like this,' Seung-chan quotes an old catchphrase and explains it using "insa", 'greeting'. The phrase "deonjineun banmyeon" means 'while throwing' or 'whereas he throws'.
입을 작게 열고 혀 짧은 소리로 발성을,

'the other opens the mouth small and vocalizes with a lisping sound,' Seung-chan details the physical acting starting with "ibeul", 'mouth', and "jakge", 'small'. He notes the "hyeo jjalbeun", 'short-tongued' or lisping, "sori", 'sound'.
'Ah, but he uses a head voice.' Seung-chan adds a surprising technical detail. He starts with "geunde", 'but', and proudly identifies the "duseong", 'head voice'.
'Not here, like this, not here.' Seung-chan quotes another famous routine. He repeatedly uses "eopda", 'is not here', demonstrating it with "ireoke", 'like this'.
'Continuously throwing questions,' Seung-chan analyzes the comedy structure using "gyesok", 'continuously'. He notes how the character is "jilmuneul", 'questions', "deonjimeyonseo", 'throwing'.
'neutralizing that system,' Seung-chan elevates the slapstick to high art. He uses "geu siseutem", 'that system', and "muryeokwasikineun", 'neutralizing'.
'if he pursues comedy.' Seung-chan concludes his deep dive with "komidi", 'comedy', and "chuguhandamyeon", 'if he pursues'. Now let's listen to the whole academic analysis again.
일단 바보 캐릭터를 비교 분석 중인데요.
입을 작게 열고 혀 짧은 소리로 발성을,
From "gongbu" for study to "bunseok" for analysis, you now have the vocabulary to discuss anything with absolute seriousness. Keep practicing!
